newsitem.title: DUBAI: French defence minister in UAE for talks.
newsitem.headline: French defence minister in UAE for talks.

text.p: French Defence Minister Charles Millon arrived in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) for talks on Saturday, the official Emirates News Agency (WAM) reported.
WAM said Millon was met at Abu Dhabi airport by the UAE Chief of Staff, Sheikh Mohammad bin Zaid al-Nahayan.
Diplomats said Millon would hold talks with UAE officials on bilateral relations, the Middle East peace process and possible arms deals.
The UAE, tied to Paris by a defence pact, is a major French arms client. France has been vying with the United States for a long-awaited Emirates order for 80 warplanes potentially worth $6 billion.

France has already supplied the UAE with Mirage planes and AMX tanks. The UAE ordered French Leclerc battle tanks worth $3.62 billion in 1993, in preference to British and American rivals, and awarded a $235 million deal to the Franco-German Eurocopter company in 1995 for new helicopters and upgrades.
